parsing.return_type: TABLE(mes_referencia date, total_creditos numeric(18, 2), total_debitos numeric(18, 2), saldo_consolidado numeric(18, 2), qtd_transacoes integer)

risks.message: Recursive CTE should stay in SQL; re-implementing it in Python is costly.
Depends on other database routines: fn_saldo_cliente.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.
Return OUT/INOUT parameters as an immutable result type.
Return RETURN QUERY rows as a sequence of typed rows.

architectural_decisions.decision: Kept the recursive months CTE, the movimento aggregate and the final join/order entirely as parameterized SQL via sqlalchemy.text().
architectural_decisions.rationale: Set-based relational logic performs best and stays closest to the database; reimplementing a recursive month generator in Python would be costlier and slower.

architectural_decisions.decision: Called once up front via a small scalar query and passed back into the main SQL as a bind parameter.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The routine depends on a database-defined function whose implementation lives outside this migration scope; calling it once avoids evaluating it inside every output row while preserving results.

architectural_decisions.decision: RAISE EXCEPTION became RelatorioError raised before any SQL; the WHEN OTHERS block became a broad except that logs a warning and executes the fallback-row SQL against the same connection.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Preserves the legacy degraded-mode contract (always returning at least one row) without swallowing the invalid-period case, which was an intentional hard failure.

warnings: In PL/pgSQL, an exception aborts the current transaction's changes within the block; here the caller owns the transaction, so after a failed main-query execution the connection state depends on how SQLAlchemy/the driver handled the error — verify whether the fallback SELECT can still execute on the same transaction or needs a savepoint/nested transaction around the main query attempt.

saldo_consolidado in the fallback path is computed from fn_saldo_cliente even though its own evaluation could have been what failed; in the worst case v_saldo_atual remains unset (None) and COALESCE(...,0) applies, matching the legacy variable default but masking the underlying balance failure.

qtd_transacoes counts all EFETIVADAS transactions touching either account side, meaning transfers between two accounts of the same client count twice toward credits/debits sums relative to net position — preserved verbatim from the legacy SQL.
If fn_saldo_cliente does not exist in the migrated schema, replace _SALDO_ATUAL_SQL with equivalent inline SQL computing the balance from contas.saldo/transacoes.
No row locking exists in the original routine; none were added. Report reflects committed/current snapshot consistent with the caller's isolation level.
